newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities end mostly higher.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities end mostly higher.

text.p: Singapore government securities ended mostly higher in moderate trade on interbank and retail interest, dealers said on Tuesday.

"The interbank rate eased slightly today but there was little impact on the market. Treasury bill yields were steady to slightly higher while bond prices were slightly higher. Volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 2.55/2.50 percent compared with Monday's yield of 2.45/2.40 percent but one-year was unchanged from Monday's yield of 2.60/2.55 percent.
Among bonds, July 1998 ended at S$97.79/97.84 against Monday's close of S$97.73/97.78, September 2001 at S$96.58/96.63 versus S$96.28/96.33 and June 2003 at S$94.58/94.63 from S$94.33/94.38.
The overnight interbank offered rate eased to 3-1/4 3-1/8 percent against Monday's 3-5/16 3-3/16 percent.
